services.name: Sengkang General Hospital (SKH) – Department of Psychiatry
services.desc: Diagnoses and treats depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety, OCD, PTSD, schizophrenia, insomnia and dementia. services.name: Khoo Teck Puat Hospital (KTPH) – Psychological Medicine

You can be referred by your primary care doctor or a lawyer, or refer yourself. Appointment phone and email per ICA. TMS referrals from other psychiatrists: ktph.psyservices@ktph.com.sg.

services.name: Woodlands Hospital – Medical Psychiatry

Bring a referral letter or doctor’s memo to your first visit. If you do not have a doctor, get a referral from a polyclinic or GP first.

The Child and Adolescent Mental Wellness Service covers mood and anxiety disorders, OCD, ADHD, autism, Tourette’s, and stress-related and psychosomatic disorders; it currently takes internal KKH referrals only. services.name: SKH – Department of Psychology

You need a referral from your GP or doctor.

services.name: TTSH – Department of Psychology
services.desc: Therapy, mostly CBT, for anxiety, mood and trauma-related disorders, grief, sleep problems, chronic pain and weight management. Subspecialties are general, bariatric, geriatric, pain, rehabilitation, trauma and sleep psychology. All referrals must come from a medical doctor; no walk-ins.

services.desc: Psychological and neuropsychological assessment and therapy for children and adolescents aged 7 to 18, and for women. Psychologists also work in KKH’s chronic pain, dermatology, diabetes and other clinics. Patients must see a KKH doctor first, who then refers them to a psychologist.

services.name: Lions Befrienders – Counselling Service
services.desc: A community mental wellness service started in 2021. It began by supporting Lions Befrienders’ own seniors and now also serves caregivers, families, youths, working adults and the wider community. Services include individual and group counselling, caregiver support, prison reintegration programmes, suicide and depression risk assessments, life-stage planning, digital counselling and mental wellness workshops. The address is the head office; the service also has other counselling offices. Email for enquiries and referrals.
services.other: Email: lbsa_counselling@lb.org.sg; Operating hours: Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm

services.name: Lions Befrienders – Befriending (Community Wellbeing and Support Services)
services.desc: Companionship for socially isolated seniors through home visits and phone calls, in areas assigned by AIC. It aims to reduce loneliness, help seniors age in place and connect them with useful help. For Singapore Citizens and PRs aged 60 and above, usually with at least one or two risk factors: living alone or effectively alone and feeling lonely; little or no social support; being the main caregiver for someone with high care needs; or limited social contact because of a physical or cognitive impairment. New befriending referrals go through AIC’s Integrated Referral Management System (IRMS) at app.aic.sg/eReg. Eligible seniors can also be invited to drop in at an Active Ageing Centre. Email for help with referrals.
services.other: Email: befriending@lb.org.sg; Operating hours: Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm

services.name: Lions Befrienders – Community Case Management Service (CCMS)
services.desc: Case management for vulnerable seniors and their caregivers who are struggling with several health and social needs at once. It helps seniors keep living at home or in the community for as long as possible and prevents or delays residential care. For seniors aged 60 and above; residents under 60 are considered case by case. Seniors must have either two or more social risks, one social risk plus a poorly controlled chronic or advanced illness, or one social risk plus a physical, mental or cognitive impairment or behavioural issues affecting daily living. Social risks include no caregiver or caregiver issues, family problems such as neglect, social isolation or low mood, and unsafe or unstable housing. West office serves Bukit Timah, Clementi and Queenstown; East office serves Changi and Tampines. Download the CCMS referral form from the website and email it to the office for the senior’s area, copying AIC at careconsultant@aic.sg.
services.other: West office; Email: ccms.west@lb.org.sg; East office; Email: ccms.east@lb.org.sg; Copy AIC on referrals; Email: careconsultant@aic.sg

services.name: Lions Befrienders – Enhanced Home Personal Care (HPC+)
services.desc: Trained care staff come to the home to help vulnerable seniors keep living there and give caregivers a break. Help includes maintenance exercises, light housekeeping, personal hygiene, recreational activities, grocery shopping and vital signs checks. Care is tailored to each senior, can change as their needs do, and includes closer check-ins and monitoring. For vulnerable seniors who need help to keep living at home or whose caregivers need support. Singapore Citizens and PRs who meet the admission criteria can apply for a government subsidy, set by a national means test. All referrals go through AIC: a doctor at any hospital or polyclinic can apply online for the senior, or families can contact AIC or visit an AIC Link branch. AIC: 1800 650 6060, enquiries@aic.sg.
services.other: Email: contact@lb.org.sg; AIC referral enquiries; Email: enquiries@aic.sg

services.name: Lions Befrienders – Active Ageing Centres (AACs)
services.desc: Drop-in social and recreational centres for seniors who live nearby. Lions Befrienders runs 10 across Singapore, each offering activities, befriending and buddying, and information and referral. Activities include crafts, exercise, cooking, drumming, Taekwondo, Korean dance, interest groups, and classes on smartphones, languages, health and law. Befriending and buddying includes home visits and phone calls. Information and referral provides guidance on schemes and grants and links to the right services. For Singapore Citizens and PRs aged 60 and above who live near a centre. Anyone can invite an eligible senior to drop in. The listed address is the head office.

services.name: Lions Befrienders – Integrated Community Care Provider (ICCP)
services.desc: A care network for seniors in each sub-region: local providers work together to keep seniors well, spot risks early and get them timely care. Lions Befrienders leads the network in four sub-regions, bringing together Active Ageing Centres, Senior Care Centres, HPC+ and home therapy with partner agencies. Sub-regions: Bukit Timah & Queenstown 4; Clementi 1; Clementi 2; Tampines & Paya Lebar 3.

services.name: Lions Befrienders – Gym Tonic (LB AAC @ Mei Ling)
services.desc: A strength-training programme that helps seniors stay strong and lowers their risk of frailty and falls. Training is tailored to each person’s fitness level and progress is tracked with software. Participants typically gain about 20% in muscle strength after 3 months. The programme is 24 sessions over 3 months, twice a week. For seniors aged 60 and above who can walk without help, follow basic instructions and attend twice a week. They should have no complications such as a past stroke, seizures or ongoing rehabilitation. Fees apply, with lower rates for Pioneer Generation, Merdeka Generation and Blue CHAS cardholders.

services.name: Empowered Families Initiative (EFI)
services.desc: A programme for lower-income, under-resourced households in Singapore that backs their own plans to improve their situation and income. EFI is a registered charity set up by social service practitioners, whose approach is: “We don’t focus on needs but on potential.” Access Grants support goals such as education or a home-based business, with families deciding how to use the funds. Savings Matching matches savings 1:2 over six months, capped at $1,200. Peer Support Networks bring families together regularly to share progress, learn from one another and support each other. For households that want support to invest in goals that can increase their income.
services.address: 25 International Business Park #04-103L, German Centre, Singapore 609916

services.name: Catholic Welfare Services – Social Assistance
services.desc: Financial and social support to help individuals become more financially and personally self-reliant. Combines short-term aid with longer-term solutions, including family interventions and referrals to external agencies. CWS also runs a bursary programme for students. Referrals must be made through the CWS Social Assistance Referral Form on the programmes page, for SSOs, FSCs and other referring agencies only.

services.name: Catholic Welfare Services – Emmanuel Second Chance Education (ESCE) Programme
services.desc: A scholarship and mentorship programme for individuals in difficult financial circumstances who need a second chance in life. Gives clients the means to earn a better income and realise their potential, funded by an anonymous donor. To apply, download the ESCE application form from the programme page.

services.name: Catholic Welfare Services – Hearts@Work
services.desc: Vocational training for young adults aged 19 to 40 with intellectual disabilities. Launched in 2009, it offers work skills training, partnerships with private companies for hands-on projects, and programmes for personal development.

services.name: Catholic Welfare Services – The Night Mission
services.desc: A volunteer-led outreach programme for people sleeping rough, which began in Bras Basah and expanded to Toa Payoh, Ang Mo Kio and Bedok. Teams visit rough sleepers and homeless individuals, provide essentials such as food, drinks and toiletries, and link people to support programmes. Focuses on befriending and respects each person’s privacy. To refer a client for shelter or support, use CWS Shelters for Rough Sleepers or Social Assistance instead. For volunteering enquiries, email volunteer@catholicwelfare.org.sg.

services.name: Catholic Welfare Services – Shelters for Rough Sleepers
services.desc: Temporary housing and social work support to help rough sleepers move towards long-term housing. CWS runs three shelters: Bethlehem Shelter in Ang Mo Kio accommodates up to 8 individuals and one family of four; S3P Shelter at Thomson (SLF Building, with MSF) accommodates up to 5 clients; Gift of Joy Shelter in Telok Kurau (with Willing Hearts) accommodates up to 16 individuals and two families of four. To refer, use the shelter referral form on the CWS programmes page.

services.name: St Joseph's Home (Catholic Welfare Services)
services.desc: A nursing home founded in 1978 with the Canossian Sisters. Provides long-term residential care, physiotherapy, occupational, art and music therapy, case management and counselling. One of Singapore’s pioneering hospice care institutions, with an on-site Childcare Centre for intergenerational activities.

services.name: St Theresa's Home (Catholic Welfare Services)
services.desc: A nursing home founded in 1935 by the Little Sisters of the Poor and managed by CWS since 2003. Houses over 200 residents and offers personalised care and rehabilitation services, including physiotherapy and occupational therapy, to help residents stay independent.

services.name: Villa Francis Home for the Aged (Catholic Welfare Services)
services.desc: A nursing home established in 1973 and managed by CWS since 2001. Houses over 240 residents and provides nursing and medical care with consultants, specialists and volunteer doctors. Physiotherapy and occupational therapy support mobility and independence.

services.name: St Vincent Home (Catholic Welfare Services)
services.desc: A residential facility established with SSVP that provides a safe, supportive home for up to 18 elderly residents. Focuses on self-sufficiency and independent living in a communal, extended-family setting. For seniors aged 60 and above who lack family support, have limited financial means and need stable housing.

services.name: CWS – BT YouthReach
services.desc: An outreach programme for at-risk youth, developed from the Poverello Teen Centre (1999) and expanded with Boys’ Town in 2009.
